summary:
Sachsen-Anhalt co-authored, with Sachsen and Thüringen, a joint Länder Bundesrat initiative (June 2026) to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act (SBGG) in the wake of the "Fall Liebich" — a convicted far-right extremist who had her legal gender changed after sentencing — proposing an abuse-review mechanism defining when registry offices may intervene in gender-marker changes, on the stated ground that self-determination rights are being "abused." The dossier describes critics' view that the initiative would restrict how trans and intersex people use the right; the SPD-led ministries consider the existing law already sufficient. No Land-specific street-attack series, police offence dataset or administrative ban comparable to Bayern's language prohibition was documented for Sachsen-Anhalt in this research pass.

National score is 0.71. Sachsen-Anhalt sits 0.03 below: the SBGG-tightening initiative is a clear legislative-hostility signal but remains an attempt, not an enacted change, and the unit lacks the physical-attack pattern of Brandenburg (0.66) or the equality-dismantling bill of Thüringen (0.65). Compared to Bayern (0.67), Sachsen-Anhalt shares the SBGG-initiative role but has no equivalent standing administrative ban affecting every public counter a visitor encounters.

sources.summary: dpa report (updated 2 June 2026): Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt and Thüringen bring a Bundesrat initiative to tighten the federal Self-Determination Act, proposing an "abuse review" mechanism with objective, documentable grounds for registry-office intervention, triggered by the Fall Liebich; backed by Union MPs, resisted by the SPD, while the federal family ministry runs a scheduled SBGG evaluation.

localsOnly: The SBGG initiative targets the legal gender-change/civil-registry procedure — machinery a visitor never uses; its visitor-facing weight is climate signalling only.
